findings.description: The schema-version-1 publication path adds tag validation but bypasses number_domain_check, which is called only by validate_candidate_v2. The documented publication number-domain contract does not exempt --allow-v1 candidates.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when an otherwise valid, approved v1 candidate contains a numeric token such as 1.0 or 1e3 and is published with --allow-v1, then this path does not reject that lexical form before publication, violating D-3.2's integer-token requirement.
findings.suggested_fix: Run number_domain_check on PUBLISH_CANDIDATE before dispatching by schema version, so both supported publication paths enforce the lexical number domain.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when an otherwise valid, approved v1 candidate contains a numeric token such as 1.0 or 1e3 and is published with --allow-v1, then this path does not reject that lexical form before publication, violating D-3.2's integer-token requirement.

findings.description: Confidence: medium (depends on one line outside the diff). The squash-trailer regex `\(#([0-9]+)\)[[:space:]]*$` is matched with `[[ =~ ]]` against the whole of MERGE_MSG. Bash ERE has no multiline mode: `$` anchors only at end of string and `[[:space:]]*` will not skip past body text. The header says the number is taken from the "subject", but the variable is the merge *message*. If the workflow passes `github.event.head_commit.message`, or the `--merge-sha` fallback at line ~84 uses `git log --format=%B`, every GitHub squash merge with a body (the default "Default message" setting appends the commit list) carries `(#NNN)` at the end of line 1, not at the end of the string, so the trailer never matches. The merge-commit regex is `^`-anchored and still works, so only squash merges regress. The new override at lines 153-156 then forces pr_type=other and the workflow guard skips full-pipeline, so a real cycle PR is silently treated as a push. The old `grep -oE '#[0-9]+' | head -1` was multiline-safe, which is why this was never visible before. The KF063 bats cases presumably pass subject-only strings via --merge-message and would not catch this.
findings.failure_mode: When MERGE_MSG contains the commit body (head_commit.message or `git log %B`) and the PR was squash-merged with a non-empty body, then PR_NUMBER is empty, pr_type is forced to `other`, stderr says "no associated PR: a push, not a merge", and neither post-merge job runs for a legitimate cycle merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Match against the subject only: `_subject="${MERGE_MSG%%$'\n'*}"` and use `$_subject` in both `=~` tests (harmless if MERGE_MSG is already subject-only). Add a KF063 bats case whose --merge-message has a `(#NNN)` first line followed by a blank line and a body, and one whose `--merge-sha` commit has a body. Confirm what post-merge.yml and the line-84 fallback actually pass.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope
findings.failure_scenario: When MERGE_MSG contains the commit body (head_commit.message or `git log %B`) and the PR was squash-merged with a non-empty body, then PR_NUMBER is empty, pr_type is forced to `other`, stderr says "no associated PR: a push, not a merge", and neither post-merge job runs for a legitimate cycle merge.

findings.description: Confidence: medium-low. `jq -r '.tag'`, `jq -r '.target_commit'` and `jq -r '.remote_push_url'` emit the literal string `null` for a missing or null field. The v1 path (`--allow-v1`) is explicitly for candidates written by the pre-cycle-133 orchestrator, whose schema this diff does not validate; if any of those keys is absent the call becomes `remote_tag_lookup null vX.Y.Z` (git: 'null' does not appear to be a git repository) and the operator sees "Cannot read refs/tags/... from null: remote unreachable, identity unverified" — a misleading diagnosis for a schema gap — and every --allow-v1 publish is refused. The same `jq -r` pattern at lines 2071-2072 (v2) is only safe if the truncated schema predicate asserts `.tag` and `.remote_push_url` are non-null strings.
findings.failure_mode: When a v1 candidate lacks `remote_push_url` (or `tag`/`target_commit`), then validate_tag_identity probes a remote literally named `null`, fails the lookup, and --publish --allow-v1 exits 2 with a 'remote unreachable' message that points at the wrong cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Read with `jq -r '.remote_push_url // empty'` etc.; if tag or target is empty, refuse with an explicit "candidate lacks <field>" message; if the URL is empty fall back to `${PUSH_URL:-origin}` (the value phase_tag will push to). Confirm the v2 schema predicate requires `.tag` and `.remote_push_url` to be strings.
findings.failure_scenario: When a v1 candidate lacks `remote_push_url` (or `tag`/`target_commit`), then validate_tag_identity probes a remote literally named `null`, fails the lookup, and --publish --allow-v1 exits 2 with a 'remote unreachable' message that points at the wrong cause.

findings.description: Both `git ls-remote` invocations in remote_tag_lookup and the `git fetch` in validate_tag_identity (line 1690-1691) send stderr to /dev/null. An authentication failure, a revoked deploy key, a mistyped `remote_push_url`, or a `timeout` kill (exit 124) all collapse into the single phrase "remote unreachable, identity unverified". phase_tag previously let git's own stderr through, so this is a diagnosability regression on the path operators must act on by hand. Separately, only ls-remote is bounded by `timeout 60`; the subsequent fetch is not, so the header's promise that a hung transport is a failed lookup holds for the first round-trip only.
findings.failure_mode: When the push destination rejects credentials (or the fetch stalls after a successful ls-remote), then the operator gets an exit 2 with no indication whether the cause is auth, DNS, URL, or timeout, and in the fetch case no exit at all until the CI job timeout fires.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture stderr (`2>"$err"` to a mktemp file or `2>&1 >/dev/null` into a variable) and append its last line to the ERROR message; distinguish exit 124 as "timed out after 60s". Wrap the fetch in the same `timeout 60` guard via a small helper.
findings.failure_scenario: When the push destination rejects credentials (or the fetch stalls after a successful ls-remote), then the operator gets an exit 2 with no indication whether the cause is auth, DNS, URL, or timeout, and in the fetch case no exit at all until the CI job timeout fires.

findings.description: The new header text says the lexical number-domain check runs "by --publish on the candidate — whether or not rfc8785 is installed", and the exit-code table lists "a non-integer number at generate or publish" as an exit-2 refusal. In the diff, number_domain_check is invoked only from validate_candidate_v2 (line 2028) and prepare_candidate (line 2106). The `--allow-v1` branch of publish_candidate gained validate_tag_identity but not number_domain_check, so a v1 candidate containing `1.0`, `1e3`, `-0`, or a number above 2^53-1 is still published.
findings.failure_mode: When a v1 candidate with a non-integer JSON number is published under --allow-v1, then it passes straight to the publishing phases and the documented integer-domain contract is not enforced on that path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `number_domain_check "$PUBLISH_CANDIDATE" "" || return 2` before validate_tag_identity in the v1 case, or narrow the header/exit-code text to say the integer check applies to schema_version 2 only.
findings.failure_scenario: When a v1 candidate with a non-integer JSON number is published under --allow-v1, then it passes straight to the publishing phases and the documented integer-domain contract is not enforced on that path.

findings.description: The pre-write check consults the remote named by the candidate's `.remote_push_url`, while the re-check and the push in phase_tag (lines 1117, 1122) use `${PUSH_URL:-origin}`. If PUSH_URL is not populated from the candidate before phase_tag runs (not visible in this diff), the two identity checks and the push itself can target different remotes: the pre-write refusal could pass against the candidate's URL while the race re-check and push go to `origin`, or vice versa, defeating the 'identical identity → skip push' logic.
findings.failure_mode: When `.remote_push_url` and `${PUSH_URL:-origin}` resolve to different remotes, then validate_tag_identity verifies one remote, phase_tag re-checks and pushes to another, and a tag of another identity on the actual push destination is detected only at push time (exit 1, state FAILED) rather than refused pre-write (exit 2).
findings.suggested_fix: Derive one URL once in publish_candidate (`PUSH_URL=$(jq -r '.remote_push_url // empty' ...)`; fall back to origin) and pass that same variable to both validate_tag_identity and phase_tag, or assert in validate_candidate_v2 that the candidate URL equals the URL phase_tag will use.
findings.failure_scenario: When `.remote_push_url` and `${PUSH_URL:-origin}` resolve to different remotes, then validate_tag_identity verifies one remote, phase_tag re-checks and pushes to another, and a tag of another identity on the actual push destination is detected only at push time (exit 1, state FAILED) rather than refused pre-write (exit 2).
